guide:mechanic:stat:Reaction%20%5BX%5D%2.description:
When specific trigger X has been met, perform Y ability immediately after the resolution of the triggering ability
- Note: The trigger types are as follows:
* On PDamage Taken - Triggers when taking Physical damage
* On MDamage Taken - Triggers when taking Magical damage
* On Near Death - Triggers when dropping to/below 25% of max HP
* On PHit Dodged - Triggers when evading a Physical ability
* On PCrit Taken - Triggers when taking a Critical Hit from a Physical ability
* On Each Turn - Triggers at the combatant's start-of-turn
* On Killed - Triggers when the combatant is reduced to 0 HP
* On Damage Taken - Triggers when taking any ability damage
* On Skip Turn - Triggers when choosing the Skip Turn command
* On Healing Taken - Triggers when receiving healing from an ability
* On PAbility Used - Triggers after the resolution of any Physical ability used by the combatant
* On MAbility Used - Triggers after the resolution of any Magical ability used by the combatant
* On Healing Used - Triggers after the resolution of any ability that resulted in healing used by the combatant
* On PCritGiven - Triggers when dealing a Critical hit with a Physical ability
* On Basic Ability Used - Triggers after the resolution of any ability flagged as Basic used by the combatant
- Note: Reactions that happen simultaneously form a queue per-combatant per-trigger; the order in which queues execute is the same as the order of the triggers they follow (generally, this order is informed by turn \> hit effect \> ability resolution).
On Killed is special in this regard in that it skips the line - it gets shoved to the front of the queues for processing before other queues are evaluated. The intended use case is for combatants revived with Re-Raise to use reactions that would require them to be alive.
For simultaneous Reactions with the same trigger (in one queue), the order is first determined by the ID of the model in which those Reactions originate, then the order in which they appear in that model.
When multiple queues from different combatants are asserted in response to any particular action, the priority layer looks like this:
* The player party always gets first priority for queue processing, even if the triggering ability originated from a player. This means that for each trigger, all player combatants process their queues first - then enemies process theirs.
* Within each party, the index order of its combatants determine who processes their reactions first; for the player party, member 1 goes first, then member 2, etc. For the enemy party, enemy 1 goes first, then enemy 2, etc.
- Note: The following Reactions (the abilities they respond with) do not trigger other Reactions:
* OnPDamageTaken
* OnMDamageTaken
* OnPHitDodged
* OnPCritTaken
* OnDamageTaken
* OnAbilityUsed
* OnHealingTaken
* OnPAbilityUsed
* OnMAbilityUsed
* OnHealingUsed
